title: chargehand local profile, v1
description: Environment-specific settings. Your own lives in profiles/local.json (gitignored), and every field is optional (ADR 0026) — chargehand runs with none at all. Secrets are referenced by item name, never stored here.

runtime.description: Names the runtime to drive (ADR 0026); wins over CHARGEHAND_RUNTIME. Unset: the profile's only runtime block (opencode or claude_code) names it (ADR 0032); with none or both, PATH is probed for a known agent CLI — none found or more than one found is an error.

secrets.description: Ordered secret lookup (ADR 0026): the first source that resolves an item wins. Default with no profile: env only. A profile still carrying "secret_store": "keychain" needs the one-line migration to an explicit command entry shown in example.json.

env.description: Look up the item as an environment variable (uppercased, - to _).

command.description: Argv run directly via Process, no shell; "{item}" is substituted per array element.

url.description: The orchestrator's own OpenCode server, bound to loopback.

binary.description: Pinned OpenCode binary the launcher starts.

version.description: Expected /api/info version; the adapter refuses to run on a mismatch.

claude_code.description: Claude Code CLI as the worker runtime (ADR 0020). When set, it is used instead of opencode. At most one credential; with neither, the CLI's own signed-in login (--setting-sources "").

version.description: Expected `claude --version`; the adapter refuses to run on a mismatch.

api_key_secret.description: Secret item holding ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: per-token billing, workers run with --bare.

oauth_token_secret.description: Secret item holding a `claude setup-token` OAuth token: the owner's subscription limits, workers run with --setting-sources "".

base_url.description: Anthropic-compatible gateway the workers call (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL). Unset: Anthropic directly; an inherited ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is ignored.

worker_root.description: Where worker clones and worktrees live. Must be outside the OpenCode user's home: OpenCode discovers skills by walking up from the session directory. Default (ADR 0026): a fixed directory outside $HOME, created on first use.

signing.description: Sign every result (ADR 0036). Chargehand never creates or stores a key. CHARGEHAND_SIGNING_KEY_FILE overrides key_file.

key_file.description: A P-256 private key in PEM: openssl ecparam -name prime256v1 -genkey -noout | openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -nocrypt -out signing-key.pem

support_check.description: Default true (ADR 0036): after a node, one call on the intake model judges whether the text each claim cites supports it; unsupported claims move to open_questions and the rest carry support. false: no check, no extra call.

sandbox.description: Where a writing preset's tests run (ADR 0035): the platform's sandbox, with no network and a cut environment unless allowed here.

kind.description: auto (default): sandbox-exec on macOS, bwrap on Linux, and a writing run is refused when neither is there. none: run the tests unconfined, an explicit opt-in.

network.description: Allow the sandboxed command network access. Default false; a build that restores packages needs true.

env.description: Names of environment variables passed to the command besides PATH, LANG, LC_ALL and TERM.

driven.description: Driven writing sessions (ADR 0039): each task runs in its own container and ends in a draft pull request. Off unless enabled.

max_parallel.description: Tasks running at once in one batch. Default 2.

max_parallel_total.description: Tasks running at once across batches. Default 4.

images.description: Session images by digest; nothing else may run.

outside.description: A network besides the default one that the batch's egress container joins: the one the chargehand server sits on.

mcp_forward.description: host:port of the chargehand server as the egress container reaches it. Set, a session can call chargehand for research and review; unset, it cannot.

model_url.description: An Anthropic-compatible gateway as the egress container reaches it: http://host:port/path through a forward, or https://host/path through the proxy. Set, a session gets claude_code.api_key_secret (the key the gateway issued, with a budget) and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL instead of the real credential; unset, the real credential is in the container's environment.

otlp_url.description: An OTLP/HTTP collector as the egress container reaches it, http://host:port through a forward on a port no other forward uses. Set, each session's Claude Code exports its own logs and metrics there, tagged chargehand.run_id, chargehand.task_id, chargehand.task_run_id and chargehand.trace_id; unset, it exports nothing.

network.description: Hosts added to the preset's allowlist, and how a session reaches the chargehand server.

runner.description: The runner service in front of the container engine. Absent: the server calls the engine itself (a laptop).

push_secret.description: Secret item for the credential that pushes non-default branches and opens draft pull requests.

task_source.description: How a tracker item id (a task's ref) becomes a goal: call the tool on the mcp_servers entry with {ref} replaced by the id, then read the goal from the JSON answer.

arguments.description: The tool's arguments; the string {ref} is replaced by the item id.

title.description: Dotted property names to the title string in the answer.

body.description: The same for the description; omit for a title-only goal.

repository_roots.description: Directories a request's repository may sit under; the worker reads a clone of it under worker_root (ADR 0023). "/" allows any repository. Default: worker_root alone; the CLI's run also allows the directory it was launched in (ADR 0028).

intake_model.description: Default (ADR 0026): unset — intake runs on the runtime's own default model.

run_cap_usd.description: Hard cap per run in USD; the worker is interrupted above it (ADR 0011). Default 1.00.

max_parallel_nodes.description: Worker nodes of one run that may run at once (ADR 0011 allows 2 per model). 1 keeps one worker process at a time on a host short on memory. Default 2.

run_log.description: Path of the JSONL run log. Default runs/run-log.jsonl (gitignored) in a checkout, else chargehand/run-log.jsonl under the per-user data directory.

usage_on_spans.description: Put tokens and cost on call spans (ADR 0021). Only for calls no gateway records, e.g. Claude Code on a subscription; with a LiteLLM gateway leave false (ADR 0012).

prices.description: USD per 1M tokens, keyed by provider/model. cache_write includes the provider's surcharge. Default (ADR 0026): empty — every PriceUsd lookup is unknown cost until a model is priced here.

models.description: Maps the placeholder models presets name (e.g. provider/worker-model) to your provider/model ids. An unmapped placeholder uses the runtime's default model.

http.description: chargehand serve: HTTP and MCP, on 127.0.0.1 unless listen opens it (ADR 0018, ADR 0024).

listen.description: IP address to bind. Anything but loopback needs allowed_hosts, and belongs on a private network only (ADR 0024).

allowed_hosts.description: Host names accepted besides localhost and 127.0.0.1, e.g. the server's private-network name.

api_key_secret.description: Secret-store item holding the API key every caller sends as a bearer token.

mcp_servers.description: MCP servers by name (ADR 0034), for memory providers and preset services to refer to. Nothing connects until something refers to a server. Each has exactly one of url and command. {secret:item} is allowed in header and environment values only: it is resolved through the secrets chain when the connection opens, and a server whose secret no source resolves is not connected.

url.description: A server reached over HTTP. Streamable HTTP or, for older servers, SSE (see transport). Never holds {secret:...}: put a credential in headers.

transport.description: auto tries Streamable HTTP, then falls back to SSE if the server does not support it. Name sse for a server that only speaks the older SSE transport (skips the failed first attempt), or streamable-http to never fall back. A worker granted this server through a preset's services gets Streamable HTTP for auto, since its runtime cannot fall back: name sse for an SSE-only server.

headers.description: Headers sent with every request, e.g. { "Authorization": "Bearer {secret:item}" }.

command.description: A stdio server's argv, started by chargehand. Never holds {secret:...}: put a credential in env.

env.description: Environment of the stdio server, on top of the SDK's default set (PATH, HOME and the like). Nothing else of chargehand's own environment is inherited.

prompt_enhancer.description: A prompt enhancer (ADR 0040), unset by default: an entry of mcp_servers that lists the tools enhance and feedback (whetstone's contract). A client sends it the prompt and the repository, commit, task kind and client name, shows the rewrite beside the original and sends the original unless the user accepts it; the outcome goes back through feedback. A slow, failing or unreachable enhancer means the original is sent.

deadline_ms.description: How long to wait for enhance before sending the original; default 1500. Also the deadline_ms the enhancer is told.

memory.description: Long-term memory (ADR 0034): an ordered list of providers, each an entry of mcp_servers plus a declarative mapping from chargehand's recall and retain to that server's tools. Each executed run asks every provider at once, each under its own timeout, and gives the merged facts to its nodes as unverified context labelled with the provider's name. The single-object form (backend, url, namespace) was removed; a profile that still has it fails to load.

memoryProvider.description: One memory provider. Its position in the list is its priority.

name.description: Unique in the list. The label on the provider's facts in the prompt, and in the run log and traces.

namespace.description: The value of {namespace} in the tool arguments, e.g. a Hindsight bank. Default: name. Leave it out for a server with no banks.

tools.description: The server's tools that give the provider its operations. recall is required; retain is required when retain is true; invalidate is optional and no run calls it.

max_facts.description: Facts kept per recall (default 10). Also the value of {max_facts}.

max_chars.description: Characters kept per recall, all facts together (default 4000).

max_fact_chars.description: Characters kept per fact; a longer one is cut with an ellipsis (default 600).

timeout_seconds.description: How long one recall or retain call may take before the provider is skipped (default 10).

retain.description: Write to this provider after a run: the claims whose file or commit citations resolved, with their locators, the repository and the commit; never the request or the summary. Needs tools.retain; a provider without one is recall-only.

arguments.description: The tool's arguments, as a template. A string that is exactly one placeholder is replaced by the value with its type ({tags} an array, {max_facts} an integer, {timestamp} an ISO 8601 string) and a null value drops the argument; a placeholder inside longer text is replaced as text; numbers and booleans are literal. Placeholders: recall {query} {namespace} {max_facts}; retain {namespace} {text} {context} {document_id} {timestamp} {tags}; invalidate {namespace} {id} {reason}. An unknown placeholder fails at load.

results.description: Recall only: how to read the answer. Without this block, the answer's results array is read and each element's id and text fields. A block that leaves out path reads the root.

path.description: Dotted property names leading to the array of results in the answer (structuredContent, else the first text block parsed as JSON). Empty: the answer itself is the array.

id.description: The property of each element that holds its id. A missing id becomes a hash of the text.

text.description: What makes a fact from an element (default "text"): a property name, a template over its properties ("{date}: {summary}"), or an ordered list of these. An entry is used only if every property it names is present and non-empty; the first that is used wins, and an element with none is skipped.

format.description: text takes the whole first text block of the answer as one fact and ignores path, id and text.
